user.t:
READ-ONLY research. Do not create, edit or commit any files anywhere; return your findings as text only.

Context: "scoup.ai" (repo: freight-recovery) is a pre-product venture. The wedge: an AI agent that assembles detention and accessorial evidence packets plus demand letters, tracks deadlines and files disputes for mid-market shippers and small carriers. Pricing is a contingency % of recovered dollars. Named incumbents are Cass, Trax and CTSI; likely acquirers are Cass, Trax, Descartes, project44 and FourKites. The founder is in Norway.

Task: map the competitive landscape as of late 2026 with web research (cite every source URL and date):
1. Freight audit and payment incumbents (Cass, Trax, CTSI/Tranzact, nVision, Intelligent Audit, Data2Logistics, enVista, Loop, etc.): do they recover detention and accessorials? For whom? What pricing (contingency %, per-invoice)?
2. Startups and tools specifically for detention, accessorial or claims recovery on the CARRIER side (detention tracking apps, Trucker Tools, factoring companies' detention services, TMS add-ons, AI dispute tools) and on the SHIPPER side (accessorial auditing, dock scheduling vendors like Opendock and C3 Reservations that claim to cut detention).
3. Visibility and telematics players that already timestamp arrival and departure (project44, FourKites, MacroPoint/Descartes, Samsara, Motive): do they offer detention reporting or billing? That is the biggest threat and the biggest partnership channel.
4. AI-native freight startups 2024-2026 (funding rounds, positioning): any "agentic freight ops" companies doing dispute or claims automation.
5. Europe and the Nordics: is there an equivalent market (waiting time and standing charges under CMR or contracts, Norwegian and Swedish haulage)? Who serves it?
6. Customer complaints and gaps (G2, Capterra, Reddit r/Truckers / r/FreightBrokers, FreightWaves, DAT forums): what do users hate about current audit and recovery services?

Output (≤ 900 words):
- a competitor table (name | segment | detention/accessorial? | pricing | weakness);
- the 5 sharpest WHITE SPACES where scoup.ai could stand out;
- the 3 biggest threats;
- a confidence grade (A/B/C) per claim.
No unsourced numbers.

handback.t:
STATUS: truncated, standard-depth pass (about 12 web searches, no page fetches). Read-only was honoured. I wrote no marker file and stored nothing, so the run-contract marker and the post-acceptance memory store were skipped. Screening failed: aidefence_is_safe returned "AIDefence package not available". Nothing was quoted verbatim and the record is screened=false, so treat everything as unscreened. spentUsd is unknown.

NOT RESEARCHED OR NOT FOUND, so treat as gaps:
- Direct pricing pages for Cass, Trax, CTSI/Tranzact, nVision, Data2Logistics and enVista.
- G2, Capterra and Reddit complaint text.
- Samsara and project44 trucking-detention billing specifics.
- Nordic and Norwegian detention vendors and NSAB/CMR waiting-time rules.
- Trucker Tools detention features and factoring-company detention services.
- FreightWaves 2026 coverage.

Source dates are given where the search results showed them. "(n.d.)" means no date appeared in the result.

COMPETITOR TABLE
| Name | Segment | Detention/accessorial? | Pricing | Weakness | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Freight audit and payment (FAP) vendors generally (Cass, Trax, CTSI, nVision, Intelligent Audit, Lojistic etc.) | Mid and large shippers | Accessorials are where audits recover most. Detention cannot be validated against a rate card; it needs delivery receipts, gate timestamps or address records. (kognitos.com/blog/freight-audit, n.d.; lightsource.ai glossary, n.d.) | Contingency "often 25-50%" of savings; or "$1-$5 per invoice" or a flat monthly fee (racklify.com encyclopedia, n.d.; lojistic.com/blog/freight-audit-pricing-and-benefits, n.d.) | Audits invoices, not facts on the ground; contingency pays nobody to remove the error class (kognitos, n.d.). This is a general finding, not vendor-specific. | B for the pricing ranges (marketing-blog sources); C that a given named vendor does this |
| Intelligent Audit | Shippers, including ocean | Ocean demurrage and detention invoice validation case study (intelligentaudit.com/case-studies, n.d.) | Not found | Ocean-focused example | C |
| Loop | Shippers (freight audit, now a broader logistics data platform) | Exception Agent autonomously resolves invoice discrepancies and disputes. Raised $95M Series C, Apr 17 2026 (siliconangle.com/2026/04/17/supply-chain-ai-startup-loop-secures-95m-investment/) | Not found | Not shown to cover evidence-based detention. Best-funded AI competitor. | A for the funding; B for the Exception Agent |
| Opereit (Barcelona) | Logistics operators | AI agents for carrier invoice reconciliation and claims recovery. $2.5M pre-seed from Seedcamp and Yellow, Jun 12 2026 (theaiinsider.tech/2026/06/12/opereit-raises-2-5m-to-deploy-ai-agents-against-logistics-invoice-and-claims-leakage/) | Not found | Early stage; focus is lost and damaged claims, not shown on detention | B |
| DockClock (Platform Science marketplace) | Carriers | Uses ELD data to track detention, notify and follow up with customers, and push line items to the invoice once approved (platformscience.com/marketplace/dockclock, n.d.) | Not found | ELD-ecosystem lock-in | B |
| FleetOptos (Geotab marketplace) | Carriers | Geofence-based detention tracker applying contract-specific billing rules (marketplace.geotab.com/solutions/fleetoptos, n.d.) | Not found | Geotab-only | B |
| Detention Source (app) | Carriers and shippers | Auto-detects arrival and departure at geofences and auto-invoices per customer policy (apps.apple.com/ca/app/detention-source/id6444958697, n.d.) | Not found | Small app | C |
| bubba.ai | Likely freight forwarders | Has a detention management solution page (bubba.ai/solutions/detention-management, n.d.) | Not found | Not examined | C |
| GeoStamp by WiseTech + Motive | Forwarders and carriers | Geofence timestamps used to prove detention and settle driver pay (marketplace.gomotive.com/app/geostamp-by-wisetech-global, n.d.) | Not found | Needs the Motive/WiseTech stack | B |
| Motive (own product) | Fleets | Geofencing and detention reports filtered by location (gomotive.com/blog/introducing-facility-insights/, n.d.) | Not found | Reports, not disputes or demand letters | B |
| TMW and McLeod (TMS) | Carriers | Detention tracking and alerts, and detention bills (TMW: fleetowner.com, n.d.; McLeod: mcleodsoftware.com, n.d.) | Not found | Dated; the TMS owns the workflow | B |
| SkyBitz | Trailer tracking | Detention management feature (ccjdigital.com, n.d.) | Not found | Not examined | C |
| C3 Reservations | Shipper dock scheduling | Claims up to 90% fewer detention fees; a food-distributor case study cites more than US$35k a month saved (c3solutions.[REDACTED:high_entropy].pdf, 2023) | Not found | Prevention only, no recovery; the figures are vendor claims | B that it is claimed; C that it is true |
| Opendock | Shipper dock scheduling | Claims it reduces wait times and detention fees (opendock.com/dock-scheduling, n.d.) | Not found | Same as C3 | B |
| project44 | Visibility | Detention and demurrage optimisation, but the evidence found is ocean/container: it uses custom contracts and terminal milestones (fbj-online.com, n.d.) | Not found | Ocean-focused; no road dispute filing found | B |
| FourKites | Visibility | Demurrage and detention dashboards and alerts for ocean (itsupplychain.com, Oct 19-20 2021) | Not found | Information is five years old; no road billing found | B (old) |
| Descartes MacroPoint | Truckload visibility for shippers, brokers and 3PLs | "Detention reporting" and features to reduce detention fees (Gartner and Capterra pages, 2026 listings) | Not found | Reports only; no evidence of dispute filing | B |
| Windward | Maritime AI | AI detention and demurrage automation for forwarders (windward.ai, n.d.) | Not found | Maritime only | B |
| ClaimCMR | European forwarders, 3PLs | CMR cargo claims platform (g2.com/sellers/claimcmr, n.d.) | Not found | Cargo loss and damage claims, not waiting time | B |

Samsara, Trucker Tools, Cass, Trax, CTSI, nVision, enVista, Data2Logistics, Cargofy, 5U AI and Overroute are not in the table with detention evidence. Cargofy, 5U AI and Overroute are generic freight-ops AI. Overroute raised $5.5M on Sep 9 2026 and 5U AI $3.2M (letsdatascience.com, both n.d.).

EUROPE AND THE NORDICS
- co3.io has articles on road-freight detention (Jun 9 2026) and geofencing detention recovery for forwarders (Aug 11 2026). They say most waiting-time charges are "disputed, under-recovered, or absorbed silently" because no one has trustworthy data. Grade B (vendor content).
- NSAB 2015 governs Nordic forwarding (dsv.com/nb-no/om-dsv/terms-and-conditions/nsab2015). I found no Nordic waiting-time rules or vendors. Grade C, unresearched.

CUSTOMER GAPS (US data)
- DAT survey: 84% of carriers rank detention among their top five problems, against 24% of brokers (dat.com/blog, n.d.).
- Only 3% of carriers collect detention on at least 90% of claims (ccjdigital.com, n.d.).
- Newer data: carriers invoice 75% of incidents and customers pay 55% of those invoices (fleetowner.com, n.d.).
- About two-thirds of brokers pay detention only if they can collect it from the shipper or consignee (same sources).
- A co3.io article says carriers using manual processes often capture only around 40% of the detention they're owed (Jun 9 2026).
- Grade B overall: the DAT and CCJ items are older surveys, and the dates of the others were not shown.

FIVE WHITE SPACES
1. Dispute execution after detection. Telematics apps detect and invoice; none found assembles the proof packet, sends the demand letter, tracks deadlines and escalates. Grade B.
2. Brokers' pay-only-if-collected practice. A tool built to win the shipper-side collection step targets the real choke point. Grade B.
3. Carrier-agnostic, ELD-agnostic evidence. DockClock, FleetOptos and GeoStamp are each tied to one telematics stack. A packet built from mixed sources (ELD, BOL, gate logs, rate-confirmation terms) is open ground. Grade B.
4. Small carriers on contingency. Existing detention tools are software priced per subscription (pricing not found); a pay-only-on-recovery model fits carriers with no admin staff. Grade C, since no pricing was found.
5. Europe and the Nordics. The search found no dedicated waiting-time recovery vendor, only CMR claims tooling and generic NSAB terms. This is the founder's home turf, but the rules need real legal research. Grade C.

THREE BIGGEST THREATS
1. Loop (Series C $95M, Apr 2026) already runs autonomous dispute agents and could extend them to detention evidence. Grade A on the funding, B on the capability.
2. Visibility and telematics platforms (Motive, Descartes MacroPoint, project44, FourKites, Platform Science and Geotab marketplace apps) already hold the timestamps and could add dispute workflows. Their detention features found so far are reports and alerts. Grade B.
3. Prevention vendors (C3, Opendock) shrink the problem and the pool of recoverable dollars. A TMS or FAP vendor could also bundle detention as a feature. Grade B.

Partnership channel: the same telematics marketplaces (Motive, Geotab, Platform Science) are the cheapest route to timestamp data. Grade B.

Sources are cited inline above. Contingency and per-invoice ranges come from blog sources, not vendor price lists; verify before using them in any document.
